subject: NovaMed: regional rollout terms, EU data residency and APAC failover
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Khan <anna.khan@novamed-eu.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: NovaMed: regional rollout terms, EU data residency and APAC failover

Hi Anna,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, I wanted to put the proposed path forward in writing so your procurement and cloud teams have clear expectations ahead of renewal. High level:

- Renewal term: propose 24 months to lock pricing and guarantee Dedicated capacity for the EU region.
- Residency: provision EU-hosted model endpoints (data processing and logs stay in eu-west-1).
- APAC: pilot in Singapore as a burst/failover lane (cold standby) with the option to promote to active within 30 days of load triggers.
- Upsell option: Dedicated GPU pool (x2 nodes) for predictable throughput during peak windows.

I've attached a draft renewal (renewal_draft_v3.pdf) with the adjusted term and two routing options (strict EU-only + EU-primary w/ APAC failover). Monica is cc'd for a quick runbook and ETA for the APAC pilot.

Next steps: can you confirm procurement contacts and whether a 24-month commitment is acceptable? If procurement prefers 12 months, we can model a phased capacity increase and include an incentive credit for committing to the APAC pilot within the first 3 months.

Thanks,

Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (617) 555-0182

[Attachment: renewal_draft_v3.pdf]

From: Anna Khan <anna.khan@novamed-eu.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <contracts@novamed-eu.com>, Liam Ong <liam.ong@pacmed.sg>
Date: 2026-05-03T14:38:00+02:00
Subject: Re: NovaMed: regional rollout terms, EU data residency and APAC failover

Evelyn —

Appreciate the summary. A couple of immediate questions from cloud and procurement before we loop legal:

1) SOC 2 evidence: procurement will need the most recent SOC 2 report and a short summary of controls (can you point to that or attach?).
2) KMS / key custody for EU region — we need confirmation we can use our KMS (bring-your-own-key) for model encryption in eu-west.
3) On the APAC pilot: typical traffic will be <10% initially but may spike during campaigns. Can you confirm autoscaling/bursting behavior and expected RPS per GPU node for your recommended instance type?

Cc'ing our Asia infra lead Liam so he can weigh in on the failover SLA we need. Procurement (contracts@novamed-eu.com) — could you confirm whether a 12 vs 24 month term is a hard requirement for budgeting?

Anna Khan
Head of Cloud Operations | NovaMed Health
anna.khan@novamed-eu.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Khan <anna.khan@novamed-eu.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-04T08:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: NovaMed: regional rollout terms, EU data residency and APAC failover

Anna — thanks, good questions. Quick answers below and a few follow-ups.

1) SOC 2: attaching a short SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf and a link to our compliance pack. If procurement needs the full report under NDA, we can provision that via secure portal.

2) KMS/BYOK: yes — we support customer-managed KMS for the Private deployment option. For Hosted/Dedicated we can also integrate with your cloud KMS in eu-west-1; I'll loop Rishi on DPA redlines.

3) APAC pilot sizing: for the dedicated GPU pool we typically model 250–350 RPS for small generative requests per A100-equivalent node with batching enabled. Monica has put together two capacity profiles in the runbook attached; she can confirm adjustments for your expected LLM token lengths.

Pricing note: the 24-month term lets us offer a 12% unit-price discount and reserves burst capacity. If procurement requires 12 months we can do a 12-month with an APAC activation credit (one month free on first promotion to active).

Attachments: renewal_draft_v3.pdf (updated pricing table), SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf

Proposed next steps:
- Procurement confirms term preference (12 vs 24) — Anna, are you ok to confirm or should I coordinate directly with contracts@novamed-eu.com?
- If 24 months: we'll finalize DocuSign package and schedule a technical kickoff for the APAC pilot (target week of June 7).

Thanks — Evelyn

[Attachment: SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Khan <anna.khan@novamed-eu.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Ong <liam.ong@pacmed.sg>
Date: 2026-05-05T02:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovaMed: regional rollout terms, EU data residency and APAC failover

Hi Anna / Evelyn —

Looping in a short technical runbook snippet so you can see sequencing and time estimates for the APAC pilot + EU cutover:

- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): exchange KMS access patterns + test service account (2 business days).
- Week 1 (pilot deploy): provision APAC burst nodes, deploy model variant (quantized for burst) — rolling deploy, 1 day.
- Week 2 (load validation): synthetic traffic + prefix/KV cache warm-up — 3 days.
- Week 3 (governance): validate logs and residency controls, execute failover drill — 2 days.

Important notes:
- Failover behavior is policy-driven; by default we route APAC to EU-primary for strict-residency accounts unless the customer enables cross-region KV replication.
- If you want warm standby (lower cold-start latency) we recommend a small reserved APAC pool (2x GPU nodes) which is what Evelyn priced in the renewal draft.

I've attached onboarding-runbook-v2.docx with the full checklist and the estimated runbook for model transfer and traffic cutover. Happy to do a 30-min tech sync with Liam and your infra team next week.

— Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: onboarding-runbook-v2.docx]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: contracts@novamed-eu.com, Anna Khan <anna.khan@novamed-eu.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-05T11:26:00-04:00
Subject: Re: NovaMed: regional rollout terms, EU data residency and APAC failover

Hi all —

I've reviewed the renewal redline. A couple of legal/controls items to call out before we send the DocuSign packet:

- DPA: added a short redline to DPA_amend_redline.docx that clarifies routing for logs vs. payload and confirms logging retention in eu-west-1 for the EU-hosted endpoints.
- BYOK language: we need a short ops-level runbook appended to the SLA that explains key rotation windows and emergency key-rollback procedures. This is standard and doesn't affect pricing.
- Subprocessor list: procurement asked for an up-to-date subprocessors table; we will provide the current list and commit to 30-day notice for changes.

If these are acceptable I can finalize the contract redlines and send to procurement for signature.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DPA_amend_redline.docx]

From: Anna Khan <anna.khan@novamed-eu.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <contracts@novamed-eu.com>, Liam Ong <liam.ong@pacmed.sg>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-06T16:41:00+02:00
Subject: Re: NovaMed: regional rollout terms, EU data residency and APAC failover

Evelyn —

This looks good and aligns with our risk bar. Procurement (contracts@novamed-eu.com) confirms a preference for 24 months if the 12% discount and reserved burst capacity are included. We'll proceed on that basis.

Action items for Redwood:
- Share full SOC 2 under NDA (we will ask legal for the secure portal link).
- Finalize DPA redline and append ops-level BYOK runbook.
- Send DocuSign package for the 24-month renewal and the APAC pilot addendum.

Procurement will issue PO on receipt of DocuSign. Can we target kickoff the week of June 7? Liam and I are available June 8–10 for the tech sync.

Thanks — Anna

[Procurement note: procurement team will wait for DocuSign before issuing PO]
